explanation.headline: Market has zero liquidity: no orders on either side, so nothing can be executed.
explanation.summary: The contract runs on DreamDEX and settles via a publicly auditable oracle. However, the market has never seen a trade, leaving it illiquid, with no depth or volatility data, and an elevated staleness rating. Despite that, 192 minutes (about 20% of the window) remain before expiry.

perSignal.reading: Settlement will be determined by the linked oracle and is publicly auditable.
With zero bid and ask levels, no trade can be executed at this time.
Because there are no resting orders, depth durability cannot be evaluated.
Absence of trade data means volatility cannot be measured, leaving price movement uncertainty.
Since the market has never traded, the quoted mid is just the maker's initial estimate, not a market consensus.
There are 192 minutes left in the 240-minute window, meaning only about 20% of the window has elapsed.
No fills have occurred, so order-flow based manipulation signals cannot be assessed.

signals.label: Venue
signals.finding: On the DreamDEX event-contracts venue.

evidence.question: Will BTC/USDC's price be at or above 80823.975 at unix time 1793232000?

signals.basis: Six venues carry binary rows on testnet; only one hosts real DreamDEX event contracts. The others include a zero-volume pricefeed-test series.

signals.label: Resolution
signals.finding: Bound to oracle question 17659037320372653062359775547111501884194039353372701524328896955765070242833, not voided or superseded; settlement is publicly auditable.
signals.basis: Oracle binding, supersession, void state and settlement-window lapse, measured from `expiry + settlementWindow` (the instant `voidExpired()` becomes callable) rather than from expiry. Question wording is templated and identical across markets, and the docs warn against parsing it, so it carries no signal.

signals.label: Liquidity
signals.finding: No orders resting on either side, so nothing can be executed.
signals.basis: Venue spreads measured 0.021-0.029 points (median 0.026), executable depth median 990 shares. Absolute points lead because a binary payoff is fixed at 0/1; the mid-ratio only catches the unplayable tail.

signals.label: Depth durability
signals.finding: No orders are resting on either side, so there is no displayed depth to judge the durability of.
signals.basis: Per-order `owner` and `expireTimestampNs` from getAllOpenOrdersOffChain: fields every aggregated view sums away. Measured on all 10 live markets, twice: 1 owner holding 100% of both sides, 6 orders, TTL 11-28s, 0 shares past expiry. So a ~20s quote and a sole owner are this venue's normal and cannot be the alarm; phantom depth and a sub-8s TTL are the deviations.

signals.label: Volatility
signals.finding: No trades have printed, so there is no price history to measure a move against.
signals.basis: Close-to-close between consecutive candles (buckets are per-trade, so intra-candle range is structurally zero). Measured max step 0.096-0.130 across markets with enough samples, so ~10 points is this venue's normal.

signals.label: Staleness
signals.finding: This market has never traded, so its quoted mid reflects a maker's opening guess rather than any consensus.
signals.basis: Last-trade age as a fraction of the market's own window. Measured median 0.040, p75 0.282, max 0.557. absolute age is meaningless across a venue running 5m to 24h series.

signals.label: Window
signals.finding: 672 min of trading left, 53% of the window elapsed.
signals.basis: Time to expiry, absolute and as a fraction of the window. Only `Trading` accepts orders and the transition is time-derived on-chain, so a market can lock between snapshot and action.

signals.label: Order flow
signals.finding: No trades yet, so there is no flow to assess.
signals.basis: Taker-side skew leads because depth imbalance measured 0.000 on every symmetrically-quoted market, so it cannot discriminate here. Skew ranged -1.00 to +1.00 across the venue, the widest of any metric.
